description: Bind each Issue to one stable target repository, route the full workflow lifecycle through it, and prevent repository deletion from orphaning non-terminal Issues.

tasks.title: Record durable process-manager pattern in architecture docs
tasks.description: Add the narrow durable application process-manager rule to design/architecture.md and the context map: a coordinator grain may persist only uncertain command delivery state, write at most one participant aggregate per command, live downstream of participant interfaces, and never receive callbacks or store duplicate business facts. This must precede coordinator implementation.
acceptanceCriteria: design/architecture.md names the process-manager pattern and prohibits multi-aggregate writes, synchronous participant callbacks, and duplicate business facts
design/domain-analysis.md context map records the coordinator as downstream of Issue and Project participant interfaces
No production code changes in this task
tasks.notes: Design D2 prerequisite. The coordinator (T-005) cannot be implemented until this rule is recorded.

tasks.title: Add EF migration for Issue repository projection and Project coordination columns
tasks.description: Add a stored generated IssueRow.RepositoryName column projected from Issue JSON state, a (ProjectId, RepositoryName, Status) index for deletion-blocker queries and list filtering, and ProjectRow columns for RepositoryRevision and LastRepositoryCommandJson. Follow the existing SQLite stored-generated-column migration precedent.
acceptanceCriteria: Migration adds IssueRow.RepositoryName as a stored generated column from the Issue state JSON
Migration creates index on (ProjectId, RepositoryName, Status)
Migration adds ProjectRow.RepositoryRevision (long) and ProjectRow.LastRepositoryCommandJson (nullable string)
Migration designer and MohistDbContextModelSnapshot are updated
dotnet build Mohist.sln succeeds with warnings-as-errors
Existing spec tests that clone schema via MigratedSqliteTemplate pass with the new columns
tasks.notes: Design D3. Follow AddAgentLaunchLabelComputedColumns precedent for stored generated column on SQLite.

tasks.title: Implement Issue target repository binding, reads, and API contracts
tasks.description: Make Issue.RepositoryRef non-null for new state with two resolution modes (creation-default vs stored-target). Add HasWorkflowStarted set in the same transaction as first WorkflowRunId/in_progress/IssueWorkStarted and never cleared. Add ChangeRepository(canonicalName) with IssueRepositoryChanged event, coordination revision/receipt fields, and reopen target validation. Add RepositoryName to IssueInfo/IssueReadModel from stored state, list filtering by OrdinalIgnoreCase stored name, and API create/PATCH/list/detail contracts returning repositoryName. Implement a shared credential-free Git URL normalizer with SHA-256 fingerprint for use by later tasks.
acceptanceCriteria: Issue.Create requires a resolved canonical repository name; creation with omitted target resolves the Project default
HasWorkflowStarted is set atomically with first workflow run and never cleared through terminal/reopen/stopped-run-clearing
ChangeRepository rejects when HasWorkflowStarted; validates and canonicalizes before applying any other PATCH fields
Reopen rejects when the retained target declaration no longer exists
IssueRepositoryChanged event is serialized in IssueEventSerializer, EventCatalog, and ProjectEventFeedAssembler
IssueInfo and IssueReadModel expose RepositoryName from stored state, independent of resolved Repository metadata
Issue list accepts a repository filter using OrdinalIgnoreCase on stored name, composing with existing filters
HTTP create/PATCH/list/detail return repositoryName; PATCH returns canonical casing
Unit tests cover canonical/default creation, unknown rejection, permanent lock through terminal/reopen, start-vs-reassign serialization, reopen validation, and event round-trip
Spec tests cover stored-name reads, unresolved terminal targets, composed filtering, and API contract shapes
npm test -w packages/server passes
tasks.output: Modified Issue domain, events, grain, read models, querier, API routes, and tests under packages/server/
tasks.notes: Design D1, D3. The Git URL normalizer (credential-free, versioned) is introduced here as a shared utility for T-004 alias rejection, T-006 run context fingerprint, and T-007 workspace identity proof.

tasks.title: Implement repository deletion protection with alias rejection and blocker query
tasks.description: Add remote-alias rejection to RepositoryPolicy: reject add or metadata update whose normalized remote fingerprint collides with another declared repository in the same Project. Add a committed-state blocker query on IssueRow for the canonical (ProjectId, RepositoryName) pair with backlog or inProgress status. Add an idempotent Project removal participant command that records a receipt and revision, rechecks repository invariants, and returns a distinct repository-in-use conflict when blockers exist.
acceptanceCriteria: RepositoryPolicy.BuildAdd and BuildUpdate reject a remote fingerprint that collides with another declared repository in the same Project
mo repo add/update surface the alias conflict through existing validation error envelopes
A focused query on IssueRow detects non-terminal Issues bound to a given (ProjectId, RepositoryName)
Project participant removal command is idempotent via receipt matching and stale-revision rejection
Repository removal checks existence and default first, then queries blockers, preserving not-found/default error precedence
A deletion rejected for non-terminal bindings returns a distinct in-use conflict without mutating Project or Issue state
Unit tests cover alias rejection for add and update, and blocker detection for backlog/inProgress vs done/cancelled exclusions
Spec tests cover unused deletion success, backlog/inProgress blocking, terminal non-blocking, cross-Project isolation, and default precedence
npm test -w packages/server passes
tasks.output: Modified RepositoryPolicy, ProjectGrain participant, IssueRow query, and tests under packages/server/
tasks.notes: Design D6 alias rejection + D2 Project participant. The blocker query reads committed IssueRow state (not enriched read models) to avoid workflow-health or projection staleness.

tasks.title: Implement Project-scoped binding coordinator with persisted fence protocol
tasks.description: Add a non-reentrant IIssueRepositoryCoordinatorGrain keyed by ProjectId that serializes Issue create, target reassignment, cancelled-Issue reopen, and repository removal. It persists one PendingRepositoryCommand fence, invokes idempotent participant commands, and clears the fence after a definitive result. Route the four operations through the coordinator from API routes. Add narrow participant interfaces and an ArchTest preventing bypass.
acceptanceCriteria: IIssueRepositoryCoordinatorGrain is non-reentrant, keyed by ProjectId, and persists only a PendingRepositoryCommand fence
Create, reassign, reopen, and repository removal enter through the coordinator; completion/cancellation/start remain direct
The coordinator replays any pending command before accepting a new one
Timeout, activation loss, or unknown downstream result leaves the fence in place
Issue and Project participants match receipts by command ID, reject stale revisions, and revalidate invariants
A repository-bearing PATCH carries the complete aggregate patch so an ambiguous result cannot partially commit
ArchTest ensures only the coordinator depends on the narrow participant interfaces
Coordinator grain specs use awaitable probes to force both orderings and lost-response points for create/delete, reassign/delete, and reopen/delete without wall-clock waits
Deactivation after fence persistence or participant commit verifies replay and receipt idempotency
npm test -w packages/server passes
tasks.output: New coordinator grain, participant interfaces, API route changes, ArchTest, and tests under packages/server/
tasks.notes: Design D2. The coordinator owns no business facts. Even a successful no-op reassignment records a receipt so a lost response cannot replay as a post-start lock failure.

tasks.title: Implement immutable WorkflowRun repository context with Issue-first startup
tasks.description: Add WorkflowRepositoryContext (Name, GitUrl, BaseBranch, RemoteFingerprint, RemoteIdentityVersion) to WorkflowStartInput and WorkflowRun. Refactor startup to Issue-first: resolve the target declaration and compute the workspace/fingerprint before the Issue transaction; commit IssueWorkStarted carrying the snapshot; let the durable handler call input-idempotent EnsureStarted. Add the authoritative variable overlay that replaces repository/workspace roots after all configurable layers. Convert workspace, review, cleanup, and rebase API routes to load run-owned context instead of live Project metadata.
acceptanceCriteria: WorkflowRun persists an immutable WorkflowRepositoryContext assigned at creation
IssueWorkStarted carries the repository/workspace snapshot and typed Issue context
The durable handler rereads the Issue, ignores stale events, and calls EnsureStarted idempotently
A duplicate EnsureStarted with identical input succeeds; conflicting context on the same run ID is corruption
Authoritative variable overlay replaces repository and workspace roots after template/global/project/issue/run/stage merge
Configurable variables cannot redirect repository or workspace routing
Workspace, review, cleanup, and rebase API routes load run-owned context, not live Project metadata
Cleanup succeeds after a terminal Issue's repository declaration is removed
Omitted rebase base uses the run snapshot; an explicit base is operation-local only

Spec tests cover pre-commit failure leaving Issue unlocked, post-commit failure keeping it locked, durable replay, metadata-before-start adoption, during-run immutability, later-run refresh, and variable precedence
npm test -w packages/server passes
tasks.output: Modified WorkflowRun domain, WorkflowStartInput, IssueGrain startup, durable handler, variable overlay, API routes, and tests under packages/server/
tasks.notes: Design D4. This is the largest single task: it refactors the startup topology from Workflow-first to Issue-first and introduces the authoritative routing overlay. Existing tests that assume Workflow-first startup or live-metadata review must be updated.

tasks.title: Implement run-unique Runner workspace identity and repository-scoped delivery
tasks.description: Replace Project/Issue-derived workspace paths with deterministic run-hash paths. Version the workspace marker and registry with full run/project/issue/repository/remote identity. Implement atomic bootstrap (clone to preparation directory, verify origin, write marker, rename). Expand the existing workspace query payload with expected identity fields. Validate marker and origin before every preparation, reuse, review, rebase, cleanup, or deletion. Scope the built-in project-integration lock by (ProjectId, repository name, resource). Align local and GitHub delivery inputs with the authoritative run context, removing default/main fallbacks.
acceptanceCriteria: Workspace paths are <runnerRoot>/workspaces/run-<sha256(workflowRunId)> for Issue-backed runs
The Runner recomputes and verifies the path from its root and dispatch run ID; outside-root and symlinked paths are rejected
Marker and registry entry carry workflowRunId, projectId, issueNumber, repositoryName, baseBranch, runBranch, remoteFingerprint, and remoteIdentityVersion
Absent-path bootstrap clones to a deterministic preparation directory, verifies origin, writes the marker, and atomically renames
A crash after rename is recovered by validating the final marker/origin and rebuilding the registry entry
Existing workspace queries carry and validate the full expected identity before any operation
Missing or mismatched workspace state fails before mutation; no default or main fallback occurs
The built-in project-integration lock key includes (ProjectId, WorkflowRun.Repository.Name, resource)
Local integration and GitHub PR delivery use only the authoritative run context; equal PR numbers in different repositories do not collide
Runner unit tests use fake command/filesystem boundaries for bootstrap, interruption, mismatch, normalizer conformance, symlink rejection, review/cleanup validation, and equal-PR-number isolation
npm run typecheck -w packages/runner passes
npm test -w packages/runner passes
tasks.output: Modified Runner workspace, executor, workspace-registry, SignalR handlers, delivery actions, and tests under packages/runner/; modified stage-lock coordinator under packages/server/
tasks.notes: Design D5, D6. Generic runs without repository context retain existing workspace behavior and Project-scoped locks. The workspace-query payload expansion is versioned evolution of existing operations, not a new Runner protocol.

tasks.title: Align Issue and Repo CLI with --repo and in-use deletion surfacing
tasks.description: Replace --repository with --repo on mo issue create and add --repo to mo issue update and mo issue list. Send repositoryName in create/update bodies and list queries. Render the stored target name in list and show tables even when metadata is unresolved. Ensure mo repo delete surfaces the server's in-use failure through existing envelope handling with non-zero exit and no success output. Reject --repository on all Issue commands.
acceptanceCriteria: mo issue create accepts --repo <name>; omitting it uses the default
mo issue update accepts --repo <name> for eligible reassignment and reports the canonical result target
mo issue list accepts --repo <name> to filter by stored target
mo issue show renders the target repository name in human-readable output
--repository is rejected by Issue command parsing without sending a request
List and show tables display the stored repositoryName even when metadata is unresolved
mo repo delete prints the server's in-use conflict, exits non-zero, and never reports successful deletion
Default, not-found, and no-Project deletion failures retain their distinct meanings in CLI output
CLI specs use RecordingHttpHandler and FakeFileSystem for --repo create/update/list, table rendering, old-option rejection, and in-use delete output
npm run typecheck -w packages/cli passes
tasks.output: Modified CLI issue commands, repo delete handling, table renderers, and tests under packages/cli/
tasks.notes: Design D7. The CLI does not reconstruct server errors or deletion guidance; it preserves the server's readable envelope. No --repository alias is retained.
